mcqs.question: In a circle with centre O, points A and B lie on the circumference. Which of the following line segments is a chord?

options.A: Segment AB joining two points on the circle
options.B: Radius OA from the centre to point A
options.D: Diameter passing through O and A

mcqs.answer: Segment AB joining two points on the circle
mcqs.explanation: A chord is defined as a straight line segment whose endpoints both lie on the circle. Segment AB satisfies this definition, whereas OA is a radius, the tangent touches the circle at only one point, and a diameter must pass through the centre and have both endpoints on the circle.

mcqs.question: Points C and D are marked on a circle. Which description correctly identifies the minor arc CD?

options.A: The part of the circle between points C and D
options.C: The entire area enclosed by the circle
options.D: The line through the centre and point C

mcqs.answer: The part of the circle between points C and D
mcqs.explanation: An arc is a portion of the circumference of a circle between two points. The minor arc CD is the shorter curved part of the circle connecting C and D. The straight segment CD is a chord, not an arc, and the other options describe different concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions gives the circumference of a circle of radius r?
mcqs.explanation: The circumference (the length around the circle) is calculated as 2πr. Option B is the area formula, C is not a standard formula, and D is just a length, not the circumference itself.

mcqs.learning_point: Understand the relationship between radius and diameter
mcqs.question: If the radius of a circle is 7 cm, what is its diameter?
mcqs.explanation: The diameter is twice the radius. Therefore, diameter = 2 × 7 cm = 14 cm. Option A is the radius itself, C is half the radius, and D is an area unit, not a length.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements correctly identifies the centre of a circle?

options.A: The intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of any two chords
options.D: The point where a tangent touches the circle

mcqs.answer: The intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of any two chords
mcqs.explanation: The centre is the unique point equidistant from all points on the circle; it can be located as the intersection of the perpendicular bisectors of two chords. Points on the circle, midpoints of chords, and points of tangency are not the centre.

mcqs.question: In a circle with centre O and a point P on the circumference, which statement is always true?
mcqs.explanation: A segment joining the centre of a circle to any point on the circle is, by definition, a radius. A diameter requires two points on the circle, a chord does not pass through the centre, and a tangent touches the circle at only one point without passing through the centre.

mcqs.question: Which line segment qualifies as a diameter of a circle?

options.A: A line passing through the centre and meeting the circle at two points
options.B: A line from the centre to a point on the circle
options.C: Any chord that does not pass through the centre
options.D: A line touching the circle at exactly one point

mcqs.answer: A line passing through the centre and meeting the circle at two points
mcqs.explanation: A diameter is a special chord that passes through the centre, connecting two points on the circumference. Option B describes a radius, C is just a chord, and D describes a tangent.

mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a chord of a circle?

options.A: A line segment joining two points on the circle
options.B: A line that touches the circle at exactly one point
options.C: A line passing through the centre of the circle
options.D: A line segment from the centre to a point on the circle

mcqs.answer: A line segment joining two points on the circle
mcqs.explanation: A chord connects two points on the circumference. Option B is a tangent, C is a diameter (if it also meets the circle at two points), and D is a radius.
